color.border: Use to visually group or separate UI elements, such as flat cards or side panel dividers.
color.border.accent.lime: Use for lime borders on non-bold backgrounds when there is no meaning tied to the color.
color.border.accent.lime.subtle: Use for decorative lime borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.accent.red: Use for red borders on non-bold backgrounds when there is no meaning tied to the color.
color.border.accent.red.subtle: Use for decorative red borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.

color.border.accent.orange.subtle: Use for decorative orange borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.accent.yellow: Use for yellow borders on non-bold backgrounds when there is no meaning tied to the color.
color.border.accent.yellow.subtle: Use for decorative yellow borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.accent.green: Use for green borders on non-bold backgrounds when there is no meaning tied to the color.
color.border.accent.green.subtle: Use for decorative green borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.accent.teal: Use for teal borders on non-bold backgrounds when there is no meaning tied to the color.
color.border.accent.teal.subtle: Use for decorative teal borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.accent.blue: Use for blue borders on non-bold backgrounds when there is no meaning tied to the color.
color.border.accent.blue.subtle: Use for decorative blue borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.accent.purple: Use for purple borders on non-bold backgrounds when there is no meaning tied to the color.
color.border.accent.purple.subtle: Use for decorative purple borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.accent.magenta: Use for magenta borders on non-bold backgrounds when there is no meaning tied to the color.
color.border.accent.magenta.subtle: Use for decorative magenta borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.accent.gray: Use for borders on non-bold gray accent backgrounds.
color.border.accent.gray.subtle: Use for decorative gray borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.code: Use for code block and code diff borders.
color.border.disabled: Use for borders of elements in a disabled state.
color.border.dropindicator: Use for the outline of an active, eligible drop target or a before/after insertion indicator. Geometry distinguishes an accepting area from relative insertion. Keep keyboard focus separate. Prefer maintained drag-and-drop indicators and preserve their component-owned treatments; reserved placeholder space alone does not require this feedback.
color.border.dropindicator.warning: Use for a drop-target outline or insertion indicator communicating a blocked drop instruction. Keep rejection and the displayed operation consistent; do not pair with an accepting drop-target background. Preserve maintained indicator warning treatments and separate keyboard focus.
color.border.focused: Use for the focus ring or border of an element that currently has keyboard or input focus. Do not use to indicate selection or hover alone. When an element is both selected and focused, keep its selected treatment and add a separate focus indicator.
color.border.input: Use for borders of form UI elements, such as text fields, checkboxes, and radio buttons.
color.border.input.search: Use for the border of search inputs.
color.border.inverse: Use for borders on bold backgrounds.
color.border.selected: Use for borders or visual indicators that communicate selection, such as the active tab or a selected menu item, or the opened state of a dropdown trigger. Do not use as a keyboard focus indicator; use color.border.focused for focus and preserve the selected treatment when both states apply.
color.border.brand: Use for borders or visual indicators of elements that reinforce our brand, such as logos or primary buttons.
color.border.danger: Use for borders communicating critical information, such as the borders on invalid text fields.
color.border.danger.subtle: Use for decorative danger borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.warning.subtle: Use for decorative warning borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.success: Use for borders communicating a favorable outcome, such as the borders on validated text fields.
color.border.success.subtle: Use for decorative success borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.discovery: Use for borders communicating change or something new, such as the borders in onboarding spotlights.
color.border.discovery.subtle: Use for decorative discovery borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.information: Use for borders communicating information or something in-progress.
color.border.information.subtle: Use for decorative information borders that do not need to meet 3:1 contrast requirements.
color.border.bold: A neutral border option that passes min 3:1 contrast ratios.
